nl_question: Which genes are associated with microcephaly?

pinned_entity.label: microcephaly
pinned_entity.resolution_check: NameRes /lookup?string=microcephaly rank 1 = MONDO:0001149 'microcephaly' (biolink:Disease); NodeNorm canonical = MONDO:0001149. The HPO phenotype HP:0000252 'Microcephaly' also normalizes to MONDO:0001149. Checked 2026-09-28.

predicate_note: SAME predicate as q2 (CFTR -> diseases) but with the disease pinned instead of the gene, so the query runs in the opposite pinning direction. Edge direction: Gene (subject, n1) -> gene_associated_with_condition -> Disease (object, n0 pinned). The disease-subject direction returns 0. PloverDB expands the pinned MONDO:0001149 to 12 descendant concepts (e.g. autosomal recessive primary microcephaly, isolated congenital microcephaly, HP:0000253 progressive microcephaly); 1044 of the 2301 results bind MONDO:0001149 itself. The alternative biolink:causes (Gene -> microcephaly, 47 results; ORDO 31, UniProt 7, SemMedDB 9) is more curated, but most ORDO gene nodes in it are unnormalized orphanet:/PR: ids rather than NCBIGene, which is why gold follows q2's predicate.

validation.results_count_note: 2301 results bind 1568 distinct genes (a gene appears once per microcephaly subclass it is linked to).

Gene -causes-> MONDO:0001149.note: ORDO (31) edges use orphanet:/PR: gene nodes, e.g. orphanet:121461 'assembly factor for spindle microtubules' (= ASPM)

validation.plover_build: Plover build 2026-07-24 from kg2c-2.10.2-v1.0 nodes/edges; code commit c3ec8ba (GET /code_version, 2026-09-28)

verification_guide.summary: 5 genes with distinct cellular mechanisms: ASPM (spindle-pole protein; most common MCPH gene), WDR62 (spindle/centrosome scaffold; second most common MCPH gene), MCPH1 (microcephalin; DNA-damage response and chromosome condensation), CPAP/CENPJ (centriole biogenesis), and NBN (nibrin; double-strand-break repair, syndromic microcephaly in Nijmegen breakage syndrome). Each quote names the gene and microcephaly. Each gene has a direct edge to MONDO:0001149 itself in the gold result set.
sources_used: MedlinePlus Genetics gene pages: ASPM, WDR62
NCBI Gene RefSeq summaries: MCPH1 (79648), CPAP/CENPJ (55835), NBN (4683)
verification_guide.how_to_verify_a_medlineplus_genetics_ent: Open the gene page and scroll to 'Health Conditions Related to Genetic Changes' -> 'Autosomal recessive primary microcephaly'. The quote opens the paragraph after the standard definition sentence ('Genetic changes that cause disease are called pathogenic variants.').
verification_guide.how_to_verify_an_ncbi_gene_entry: Open the NCBI Gene record. In the top 'Summary' section, the 'Summary' row holds the RefSeq summary paragraph; the quoted sentence is inside that paragraph. (Scripted fetches of www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov hit a bot check, so the curator verified the identical RefSeq summary text through NCBI E-utilities esummary, db=gene.)
verification_guide.cross_check_with_ploverdb: Each verified_answer CURIE was confirmed present in the PloverDB result set for the gold query (n0=MONDO:0001149, n1=biolink:Gene, e0: n1 -biolink:gene_associated_with_condition-> n0) on 2026-09-28, and each has at least one edge whose object is MONDO:0001149 itself (not only a subclass). supporting_edge_ids lists only those direct edges.
verification_guide.intentionally_omitted: The pilot's picks (CEP135, KIF11, TUBGCP4, TUBGCP6, NCAPH) are also in the result set and are real microcephaly genes; gold is open-world, so they are not wrong, just not in this verified subset. MedlinePlus Genetics has no gene pages for MCPH1, CDK5RAP2 or CENPJ, hence NCBI Gene for those.

curation_notes: All 2504 edges in the result set are text-mining/automated (DISEASES and DisGeNET, knowledge_level=prediction). The gold genes are correct per curated sources, but the KG support for every gene is prediction-level.

The answer set is very large (1568 distinct genes), so this question also exercises response reduction (review.md finding 2): a system that sees an arbitrary slice may pick valid but non-gold genes. verified_hit_rate is descriptive only.
NBN is linked to microcephaly through a syndrome (Nijmegen breakage syndrome) rather than isolated MCPH. It was chosen for mechanism diversity; its RefSeq summary names microcephaly explicitly.
